text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000182 bills 99215 far above expectation in every complexity tier, mostly on patients with zero or one chronic condition, and the limited records lean toward unsupported high-level coding.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share appears in every complexity stratum, including patients with no chronic conditions, so the excess is not explained by a sicker panel. Sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0088965 (back pain) and C0089057 (upper respiratory infection) look like routine visits, while high-complexity examples such as C0089782, which the records supported at high MDM, look appropriate. The documentation is suggestive but thin: only 8 documented 99215s against a high comparison rate, so the 99215 mismatch alone is weak, though C0089578, a zero-condition respiratory 99215 documented at moderate, shows the concern. The stronger documentation signal is the 99214 tier, where 7 of 16 documented claims fall below the billed level versus about 5% for comparison providers. Notes also show signs of cloning: a third flagged as duplicate, repeated visit times, and some claiming data review with no lab or test on the claim. A reviewer should first request a larger chart sample focused on 0–1 condition 99215 and 99214 visits and compare note text across visits for templated or duplicated MDM and data sections."}
